title: Titanium GPS Mount Bolt
function: Computer/GPS mount dual-fixing M5 extension bolt
alloyReason: Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V (UNS R56400) is specified for Titanium GPS Mount Bolt because its 900+ MPa tensile strength allows thin-wall tube shaping without buckling, critical for lightweight frame and component structures. The alpha-beta microstructure delivers 45% higher specific strength than 4140 chromoly steel, translating directly to gram-level weight savings where it matters. Its high-cycle fatigue endurance limit (>500 MPa @10^7 cycles) matches the pedaling load spectrum of Computer/GPS mount dual-fixing M5 extension bolt. This rationale is driven by computer/gps mount dual-fixing m5 extension bolt and specific design requirements.
process: CNC turning Swiss-type for cockpit accessory hardware geometry
Thread rolling DIN 13-1 6g for net-shape tolerance
Go/No-Go ring gauging for net-shape tolerance
surfaceTreatment: Bead blasting 120 grit Al2O3 for matte finish Ra 1.6-3.2um followed by passive oxide stabilization in DI water — tailored for computergps mount dualfixing application
commonFailures: Thread galling Ti-on-Ti assembly - prevented by MoS2 anti-seize compound and -20% installation torque — critical for computergps mount dualfixing performance

faq.q: How much weight savings does Titanium GPS Mount Bolt offer versus steel or aluminum?
faq.a: Titanium GPS Mount Bolt fabricated from Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V provides a 40-45% weight reduction versus 4130 chromoly steel (4.43 vs 7.85 g/cm³) at the same strength. Compared to 6061-T6 aluminum, titanium's 3× higher yield strength (830 vs 275 MPa) allows 50-60% thinner walls, resulting in a net weight comparable to aluminum with 4× better fatigue life — critical for computergps mount dualfixing.

faq.q: What material certifications are provided with Titanium GPS Mount Bolt?
faq.a: Each Titanium GPS Mount Bolt shipment includes EN 10204 Type 3.1 mill test certificate with chemical analysis, mechanical properties, and heat identification. Dimensional inspection reports and Certificate of Conformance (CoC) are standard. First Article Inspection Reports (FAIR) per AS9102 are available on request for computergps mount dualfixing.
